newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Burton slips despite profit rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Burton slips despite profit rise.

text.p: British fashion retailer Burton Group Plc reported a 23 percent increase in first half profits on Thursday, but doubts about future growth hit the company's shares.

The retailer, owner of Debenhams, Top Shop and Dorothy Perkins stores, reported first half profits of 108.1 million pounds ($177.6 million), up from 88.1 million a year ago. Sales, excluding its newly acquired mail order businesses, rose to 1.17 billion pounds from 1.09 billion.
But the performance was not sparkling enough for investors who were looking for reassurance that Burton could make the transition from a recovery to a growth stock, analysts said.
Traders said the shares had been bought in the run-up to the results on expectations of a strong recovery, leaving some disappointed.
"The results were virtually in line with forecasts," one dealer said. "But sentiment has turned after they had a bit of a run up before the figures."
The shares traded seven pence lower to 146.5p at 1045 GMT.

Burton, which has achieved a dramatic turnaround from troubles in the British recession of the early 1990s, said sales, excluding home shopping, were up 6.8 percent in the first 10 weeks of the second half. Debenhams sales were up 10.9 percent over this period.
Burton, with the second biggest market share in clothing after Marks and Spencer Plc, has successfully rebuilt gross profit margins and revamped its womenswear chains to boost profits.
The company was optimistic it could keep growing, but saw a slower pace of improvement in gross margins.

Finance director Andrew Higginson said: "We've just announced a 23-percent increase in profit before tax which is another increase on a very good year last year so...fingers crossed we seem to be still delivering."

Higginson told Reuters the group had had a good run on boosting gross margins for the last three or four years. "I think there is still some scope for gross margin improvement, but it's probably going to be gentle now as opposed to dramatic."
Gross margins rose by one percentage point in the first half.
Last year Burton joined a growing list of retailers eager to capitalise on the fast growing direct mail market, following the success of retailing rival Next Plc's Directory.

The company bought two catalogue firms, Innovations and Racing Green, and is in the process of integrating them. Racing Green will be developed by its Principles fashion chain, Hawkshead catalogue by Burton Menswear and Innovations by Debenhams.

Higginson said there were plans to launch catalogues of Burton brands such as Dorothy Perkins and Evans by the autumn. He was optimistic about prospects for mail order as an extension of the store brands.

The group also announced plans to add 25 percent more space to its flagship Top Shop store at Oxford Circus in central London. Debenhams, which has 92 stores in Britain, will open nine more outlets over the next four years, creating 3,400 jobs throughout Britain.

Higginson said the revamp at Top Shop would include cafes and fashion features. U.S. sportswear maker Nike will take 70,000 square feet on the Regent Street side of the site and open the first NikeTown sportswear shop in Europe.
"To put Nike in the same building will mean there will be a huge number of people wanting to go there - so both should feed off each other," Higginson said.
All Burton's retail businesses increased profits in the half year, except Burton Menswear, which saw profits fall to 3.8 million pounds from 6.1 million.

Higginson said the menswear market in general was proving much tougher for retailers than womenswear. But the group would continue to try and improve its performance. "We've got the largest menswear brand and we'll build on that," he said.
The company has tested out a new format called "Style Union" which brings more brands into a store and it will probably test out a few more. "We are learning from that," Higginson said.
Debenhams boosted sales by 9.4 percent in the first half and the multiple fashion chains by 5.8 percent.
($ = 0.608 British Pounds)
